description:
An integrator alone does not make a transient simulator. Transient behaviour comes from state that accumulates: mass, energy and momentum holdup inside vessels, drums, columns and pipes.

SCOPE: add inventory state to the unit operations that need it — separator and vessel liquid level, column stage holdup, pipe line-pack, heat-exchanger metal thermal mass — and integrate those states rather than solving them algebraically. Steady state must fall out as the zero-derivative limit, which is a directly testable property.

TEST THIS PROPERTY EXPLICITLY: a transient run started from the converged steady state and held at constant boundary conditions must stay at that state. Any drift is a conservation bug in the integrator or the holdup terms.

Depends on the flowsheet data model and the integrator.
title: refinery: dynamic unit-operation holdup and inventory — what actually makes it transient

design:
Part of the phase 2 dogfooding programme (epic: bn op-igib).

## The dogfood task

Give a fresh Haiku agent, working from the public API only:

> Using only the public API, generate a representative random packed bed of
> equal spheres suitable for an HTR pebble bed. Target a packing fraction of
> approximately 0.61. Inspect the resulting packing, calculate the achieved
> packing fraction and minimum centre-to-centre separation, and report any API
> friction encountered.

The agent should be able to write something conceptually as simple as:

```rust
let bed = PebblePacking::new(..)
    .target_packing_fraction(0.61)
    .seed(..)
    .generate()?;

println!("{}", bed.packing_fraction());
```

The exact API need not match this sketch — **prefer the terminology and
abstractions already natural to the crate** over imposing this shape.

## Where the implementation actually is — check before assuming

A quick look before filing (2026-09-05): packing is **not** in
`outram-park-fork-liggghts`. It is in
`crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/crp_packing.rs`, a Jodrey-Tory
collective-rearrangement algorithm, alongside an RSA implementation in
`sphere_packing.rs`.

That matters for this issue in two ways: the dogfood target is `outram-mc-libs`
rather than the DEM crate, and **whether pebble packing belongs in the MC crate
or the DEM crate is now an open architectural question** rather than something
to settle by default. DEM-settled beds and CRP-generated beds are different
things with different validity claims.

## Verify the ~0.61 claim — do not take it on trust

The belief is that ~0.61 has already been reached somewhere in the
implementation or history. **This must be independently reproduced, not
assumed.**

What the source currently says, which is suggestive but not evidence of an
achieved run:

- `MAX_PF_CRP = 0.62` — documented as "a conservative, reliably-reachable
  ceiling"
- module docs cite "~0.55-0.62 fractions RSA cannot [reach]"
- RCP limit for equal spheres given as ~0.64
- RSA's own ceiling (`MAX_PF_RSA`) noted as far below ~0.60-0.61

Search tests, examples and git history for an actual measured result, and
reproduce it.

## Required verification for the produced bed

- requested packing fraction
- achieved packing fraction
- sphere count
- sphere diameter / radius
- domain volume
- occupied sphere volume
- minimum centre-to-centre distance
- **absence of overlaps within numerical tolerance**
- **containment inside the specified domain**
- **deterministic reproducibility for a fixed seed**
- runtime

**If ~0.61 cannot be reproduced, report exactly what is obtained and
investigate — do not adjust tolerances or swap algorithms to reach the
number.** A packing fraction that only appears after the acceptance criterion
is loosened is not a result.

## API requirement

**These diagnostics should be public.** A user must not have to reconstruct
packing fraction, minimum separation or overlap status from private data
structures. Phase 1's recurring finding was public types that dead-end with no
reachable operation; this is exactly that shape.
title: Pebble-packing dogfood, and independently verify the claimed ~0.61 packing fraction

description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, first comment: 'I want an interface where I draw a box on a pdf or PNG, then right click, and I can digitised a plot. That should bring me to a plot digitiser interface (popup window? Or new tab?) that after I'm done, I close. I can then preview the csv and copy/paste and/or export'). Depends on op-95x6 (the PDF reader view this interaction lives inside).

SCOPE: on the PDF reader page (or a loaded PNG), let the user drag a selection rectangle, right-click it, and choose 'Digitise plot' -- opens the EXISTING digitiser engine (crates/kovan-literature/src/digitiser/{auto,calibration,trace,dataset}.rs, already used by kovan-gui/kovan-digitise-gui) pre-loaded with the cropped region as its plot image, in a popup window or new tab (maintainer left the choice open -- note which was picked). Closing it returns to the reader.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD: the digitiser engine itself (auto-trace, calibration, hand-correction, DigitisedDataset export) already exists and is verified (see the workspace CLAUDE.md 'Graph digitisation: dogfood kovan-digitise' section) -- this bead is UI wiring (crop region -> feed as image::DynamicImage into the existing desktop::DigitiseApp -- or equivalent -- rather than a file path) and the popup/tab launch mechanism, not new digitisation logic.

CSV preview/copy/export: see op-9c2e's CSV-preview bead (shared with the table-digitiser path, filed once both producers exist).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented: PDF reader gained a 'Digitise plot (draw box, right-click)' tool (AnnotationTool::CropForDigitise in gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs) -- drag a rectangle on the current page/image, right-click inside it to confirm. On confirm, crop_current_page() re-rasterizes the current PDF page (or reads the already-in-memory PlotRaster for a directly-opened image) and builds a standalone PlotRaster via PlotRaster::from_rgb_fn over just the cropped region -- reuses the EXISTING digitiser engine unchanged (auto-trace, calibration, hand-correction, export), no new digitisation logic, per the bead's own 'reuse, do not rebuild' scope note. DigitiseApp::load_image_from_raster (new, refactored out of load_image's shared set_raster() logic) takes the crop directly -- no file path needed since it's an in-memory region, not a file on disk. The view switch doubles as the 'popup window or new tab, close when done' the maintainer described: cropping switches the window to the Digitiser view; switching back to PDF Reader is the 'close' step, so no separate popup/tab was built. Verified: cargo check clean both targets, cargo test --release -p kovan clean (160+15+17+7 passing).

title: kovan-gui: draw-box + right-click -> plot digitiser, launched pre-cropped from the PDF reader

description: v2 duplicates ~3000 lines of v1's physics (full_simulation/mod.rs 2085, heat_transfer_solvers.rs 683, fluid_solvers.rs 237, diagnostics.rs 52) because those live in a tuas EXAMPLE directory and cannot be imported across crates. Proper fix: promote educational_ciet_loop_version_4 + its three helper modules into the tuas library under pre_built_components/ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_4/, parameterised over a state type, then have BOTH v1 and v2 call it. Deferred deliberately: doing it now would mean refactoring v1, which was out of scope for the v2 request. Blocked on the port-equivalence check landing first, so there is a regression gate before the de-dup.
title: De-duplicate CIET loop: promote v4 solver into the tuas library
